questions.q: Why do Elastic Jobs exist, per this lesson's connection back to Lesson 59?
options: Because SQL Server Agent doesn't run as a full on-server scheduler inside Azure SQL Database, leaving a real gap for running scripts across many databases
Because T-SQL stored procedures cannot run inside Azure SQL Database
Because Elastic Jobs is required before any database can be created
Because SQL Server Agent was fully removed from every Azure SQL offering including Managed Instance
questions.explain: Elastic Jobs fills the specific gap Lesson 59 identified: Agent's limited role inside Azure SQL Database itself.

questions.q: What are the three pieces of an elastic job, per this lesson?
options: The job agent database, the target group, and the job (script + schedule)
The firewall rule, the VNet, and the private endpoint
The backup, the restore, and the verification step
The login, the user, and the role
questions.explain: These three pieces together let one script run against many databases on a schedule.

questions.q: Where do the jobs.sp_add_job and jobs.sp_add_jobstep procedures actually execute — inside which database?
options: Inside the job agent database, not inside the target databases being maintained
Inside every target database simultaneously as a schema change
Inside the Azure Resource Manager control plane, not any SQL database
Inside master on the on-premises SQL Server instance
questions.explain: The jobs schema and its procedures live in the dedicated job agent database, which stores metadata, not application data.

questions.q: What happens to an existing weekly job when a new database is added as a member of its target group?
options: The job automatically runs against the new database too, with no change needed to the job definition itself
The job must be deleted and completely recreated from scratch
The job stops running against all databases until manually re-enabled
Nothing changes until the job agent database is rebuilt
questions.explain: Jobs point at target groups by name — adding a member to the group extends the job's reach without editing the job.

questions.q: What kind of T-SQL does an elastic job step's @command parameter actually run, per this lesson's example?
options: A call to an existing stored procedure, such as a maintenance procedure already written in an earlier lesson
A brand-new scripting language unique to Elastic Jobs
Only Azure CLI commands, never T-SQL
Only PowerShell cmdlets, never T-SQL
questions.explain: The lesson stresses that Elastic Jobs reuses existing T-SQL skill (like the Lesson 53 maintenance procedure) rather than requiring new scripting knowledge.
